intro: Kaštela, the string of seven towns between Split and Trogir, protects two old trees as natural monuments. In Kaštel Štafilić grows Mastrinka, an olive the tourist board puts at more than 1,500 years old, its trunk 6 metres round, protected since 1990. In Kaštel Gomilica a downy oak stands beside the Romanesque church of St Cosmas and Damian, built between 1138 and 1160, protected since 1996. A reader sent us the photograph of the olive.
meta_description: Kaštela's protected trees: Mastrinka, an olive over 1,500 years old in Kaštel Štafilić, and the oak by the 12th-century church in Kaštel Gomilica.
question_meta: Kaštela's oldest tree is Mastrinka, the olive of Kaštel Štafilić, more than 1,500 years old by the tourist board.
question_answer: The oldest tree in Kaštela is Mastrinka, the olive of Kaštel Štafilić, which the town's tourist board puts at more than 1,500 years old, with a trunk 6 metres round. Croatia has protected it as a natural monument since 1990.
question_context: Kaštela's tourist board puts this olive at more than 1,500 years old. Locals call it Mastrinka, and it grows in Kaštel Štafilić, one of the seven little towns strung along the bay between Split and Trogir. Croatia has protected it as a natural monument since 1990. The town gives its trunk as 6 metres round, its crown as 22 metres across and its height as 10 metres, and says its roots reach out more than 100 metres. It still bears small olives of an oil variety. A reader who sent us its photograph wrote: "Over 1500 years old, huge olive tree (Olea europaea), majestic, maybe planted by Romans." Their picture shows why. The trunk is not one trunk but a knot of grey, ribbed columns twisted around a hollow heart, and from it limbs as thick as a body loop out and down before they climb again into a crown of silver-green leaves. It stands on a lawn behind a low railing, where the town has set up benches and information panels for visitors. Mastrinka grows beside the Maslina kindergarten, so if the gate is shut, look from the railing.

faq.q: Where is the old oak in Kaštela?
faq.a: In Kaštel Gomilica, beside the Romanesque church of St Cosmas and Damian, built between 1138 and 1160.

faq.q: How old is the Kaštel Gomilica oak?
faq.a: Nobody has published an age, height or girth. It has been protected as a natural monument since 1996.

faq.q: How do you get to Kaštel Gomilica?
faq.a: It is on the local bus line between Split and Trogir, one of the seven towns of Kaštela along the bay.

trees.name: The oak of St Cosmas and Damian, Kaštel Gomilica

location.address: By the Romanesque church of St Cosmas and Damian (Sv. Kuzma i Damjan), Kaštel Gomilica

location_site.name: Church of St Cosmas and Damian, Kaštel Gomilica

trees.story:
Kaštela's tourist board singles out this downy oak for two things, its beauty and its size, and gives a number for neither. Croatia has protected it as a natural monument since 1996, entered in the register simply as the oak in Kaštel Gomilica.

What stands beside it is far better documented than the tree. The Romanesque church of St Cosmas and Damian was built between 1138 and 1160 over the remains of a late-antique basilica, and the oak grows at its side. The church has a construction date, a style and a history of the building underneath it. The oak has none of those on paper. How long it has kept the church company is something nobody we can find has written down.

We do know it is alive. A naturalist photographed it in November 2024 and logged it a few metres from the register's own point, which settles which tree the town means and confirms it is a downy oak.

Kaštel Gomilica is one of the seven towns of Kaštela, on the local bus line between Split and Trogir, so this is an easy stop on the way along the bay.

Nobody has published its height, girth or age. If you visit, a photograph and a rough idea of its size would be the first of each that anyone has shared.

trees.access: Free to see: it stands by the Church of St Cosmas and Damian in Kaštel Gomilica. No access terms are published.
trees.transport: Kaštel Gomilica stop on the Split to Trogir local bus, roughly 25 to 35 minutes from Split (times not confirmed); walk from the stop not confirmed.
trees.how_to_recognise: You can recognise it as the large downy oak right beside the Romanesque church of St Cosmas and Damian in Kaštel Gomilica.
trees.verify_notes: REGISTER: Bioportal ps.4722 'HRAST U KAŠTEL GOMILICI', spomenik prirode, register date 1996-04-04 (one search summary of a local-heritage PDF said designated 10 December 1995 and 700 to 900 years old with a King Zvonimir legend; the PDF itself was NOT fetched, so the age, the date and the legend do not exist for us; do not use). SECOND SOURCE: kastela-info.hr/en/natural-heritage names it Quercus pubescens Willd., 'by the Romanic church of St. Kuzma and Damjan in Kaštel Gomilica', notable for beauty and size, no figures. ALIVE and PIN: iNaturalist research-grade Quercus pubescens ('Hrast medunac') observation 250913293 of 2024-11-08, 4 m from the register point (GPS accuracy 17 m); lifecheck RECENT. Register point and iNat agree within 4 m, marked confirmed; the register name gives no species, the Quercus pubescens id comes from the town page and the iNat observation. No girth or height from any fetched source. One source only gives the species, so keep flagged and ask the reader for size.
